title: Why Garlic and Onion Works So Well Together
flavorProfile: Garlic brings a sharp, pungent heat that mellows into a sweet, caramelized note when cooked, while onion contributes layers of sweetness, mild acidity, and a subtle vegetal umami. Together they create a balanced sweet‑savory foundation: the garlic’s sulfur compounds amplify the onion’s natural sugars, and the onion’s moisture tempers garlic’s intensity, resulting in a harmonious depth that supports both rich fats and bright acids.
nutritionalSynergy: Both Allium species are rich in organosulfur compounds (allicin in garlic, quercetin in onion) that synergistically boost antioxidant capacity and support cardiovascular health. The vitamin C in onion enhances iron absorption from garlic’s trace minerals, while the prebiotic fibers (inulin) in both improve gut microbiota diversity, leading to better nutrient bioavailability and immune function.
prepTechniques: Start with a gentle sweat: cook diced onion in a splash of oil over medium‑low heat until translucent, then add minced garlic for the last 30‑45 seconds to prevent bitterness and preserve aromatics.

If caramelizing, increase heat gradually after the onion is soft; add a pinch of salt to draw out moisture and a splash of wine or balsamic to deglaze, allowing the garlic to brown slowly and develop nutty sweetness.
Finish dishes by folding in a butter‑herb emulsion or a drizzle of infused oil just before plating; this re‑introduces fresh garlic aroma and a glossy sheen that highlights the sweet onion base.

prepTechniques.q: How to store leftovers made with Garlic and Onion?
prepTechniques.a: Cool the cooked mixture to room temperature within two hours, then transfer to an airtight container. Refrigerate for up to 4 days or freeze in portioned bags for up to 3 months. Reheat gently to avoid over‑cooking the garlic.
